study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissimilarity in Sulcal Width Patterns in the Cortex can be Used to Identify Patients With Schizophrenia With Extreme Deficits in Cognitive Performance

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Apply a PBSI-based normative modeling approach to sulcal width (PBSI-SW) on longitudinal MRI data to quantify individual deviance relative to healthy controls and test whether markedly deviant patients show distinct cognitive performance and sulcation characteristics.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Utrecht Schizophrenia Project; Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The supplementary material clearly states that participants were selected from two cohorts: the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, both located in Utrecht, the Netherlands. Both cohorts provided patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Participants for the current study were selected from a large longitudinal sample based on two cohorts including patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls, the Utrecht Schizophrenia project and the Genetic Risk and Outcome of Psychosis (GROUP) consortium, in Utrecht, the Netherlands.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: A small subset of schizophrenia patients exhibited marked PBSI-SW deviance linked to poorer cognition and reduced sulcation; group trajectory differences were driven by these outliers.
